headline: 2% Salicylic Acid, made for combination & oily skin

callouts.text: Penetrates the pore lining to scoop out sebum
RonaCare Salicylic Acid Extra Pure, from Merck, Germany
EGCG from green tea helps soothe inflamed skin
97% subjects said skin felt less oily all day at 2 weeks*

footnote: *Minimalist consumer study; % of subjects who reported this after using the serum for 2 weeks. Patch tested under dermatologist supervision. PM use; start every alternate day.
layout_description: Square 1080x1080. Headline top-left in dark green, two lines. Real product photo (serum bottle, upright) in the right 45% of the frame, vertically centred, with a soft shadow. Four callout labels stack down the left half in dark-green regular weight, each joined to the bottle by a thin mint leader line ending in a small dot on the pack. The fourth callout (the 97% stat) is set slightly bolder with the numeral enlarged. Footnote in small grey text along the bottom-left. 'Shop now' as a small dark-green outlined button bottom-right under the product.
image_prompt: Square 1080x1080 background-only scene. A clean, calm editorial desk setting reduced to essentials: a matte off-white tabletop meeting a soft mint-tinted off-white wall, with a single small sprig of green tea leaves resting at the far left edge, slightly out of focus. Soft, even natural window light from the left, low contrast, very gentle shadows. Palette of off-white, soft mint and a touch of deep green; clinical, calm, trustworthy mood. Keep the right 45% of the frame completely clear and evenly lit, and keep the left 50% smooth and low-detail apart from the small leaf sprig at the extreme edge. No product, no bottle, no packaging, no text, no letters, no logos, no people, no faces, no skin, no hands; also no lab coats, no badges, no certificates. Empty space reserved for the product photo and copy to be added later.
adaptation_notes: Kept: a skin-type callout aimed at oily skin, an editorial and quiet product presence, the clean white/green/mint clinical palette, and a shop-now CTA. The expert's on-camera 'advice' is rebuilt as calm ingredient callouts pointing at the pack, plus one consumer-study stat with its qualifier in the footnote. Dropped: the doctor on camera and the named-doctor badge (an expert endorsement needs a real, consenting expert; none is in the facts); the 'your moisturizer might be the problem' problem-first hook (a fear-style hook, and the claim isn't in our facts); video format (rebuilt as a static); the Oligopeptide-10 callout (a drug-style claim a cosmetic ad can't make), replaced with the salicylic acid sourcing fact (F8). Note: the match is low; the competitor sells a moisturizer and this is a serum, so the copy speaks to oily skin rather than to moisturizers.

verdict.label: Ready for human review (limited check)
verdict.detail: No rule hits. The model layer did NOT run, so implied claims and overall tone were not assessed — the reviewer must read for those.

findings.fix: State it as on the pack: 'Niacinamide 10%'.

findings.message: Statistics need their study qualifier on the creative and must not be worded more strongly than the study.
findings.fix: Quote the stat exactly as the study states it ('90% subjects said…') and add a footnote: study type (consumer perception / in-vivo / in-vitro), duration, and n if known.
findings.note: Wording appears on the product page (F17). Severity lowered one step: the brand has published it, but a reviewer must still confirm substantiation is on file.
